steps.prompt: Imagine a world where one thing works differently from ours. What is it? (Maybe it rains upward, or cats run the post office.)

cards.title: World-building
cards.body: World-building means inventing a place and how it works: its rules, its people and its everyday life. Fantasy and science fiction writers do it, but so does anyone who invents a town, a school or a planet.

cards.title: Explain it or show it
cards.telling: In this world, there was no gravity at night.
cards.showing: Every evening, Ezra tied his shoes to the bedpost, buckled his seatbelt blanket, and watched his socks drift towards the ceiling.
cards.note: The second version shows the rule through ordinary life. The reader works out the rule, and believes it.

cards.title: Everyday details sell the world
cards.body: What do people eat for breakfast? How do kids get to school? What is a normal annoying chore? Small, ordinary details make a strange world feel real.

cards.title: Find the world clues
cards.prompt: Tap the three words that show this is not our world.
cards.text: Mira fed the dragon its morning coal, then flew her broom past the floating market to school.

prompts: What is the one rule that makes your world different?
Which everyday detail makes your world feel most real?
